normative_extracts.quote: If a script is trusted via a cryptographic nonce or hash and 'strict-dynamic' is present, trust propagates to any parser-inserted or dynamically appended child scripts it creates, while host allowlists are ignored.

pipeline_phases: strict-dynamic Trust Propagation Across Dynamic Imports
engine_internals.mechanism_summary: The HTML parser and script loader compare each <script nonce> attribute against the response header's one-time random token, propagating trust to dynamically loaded chunks under 'strict-dynamic'.

production_failures.symptom: All scripts blocked in production when a CDN caches an HTML response with a static nonce
production_failures.root_cause: Nonces must be cryptographically random per HTTP response; caching HTML or hardcoding nonce='1234' lets attackers reuse the known nonce.
production_failures.mitigation: Generate a fresh 128-bit base64 nonce per SSR/edge response, or use script hashes for static CDN-cached HTML.

production_failures.symptom: CSP blocks dynamically loaded ES module chunks despite host allowlists
production_failures.root_cause: Missing 'strict-dynamic' forces every dynamically appended <script> to match brittle domain allowlists.
production_failures.mitigation: Use script-src 'nonce-<random>' 'strict-dynamic' and attach the nonce to the root entry <script>.
